name: Blackberries
desc: Bramble-picked and still warm. Half of them never make it to the bag, and that's fine.

name: Sloes
desc: Blue-black and sour enough to turn your face inside out. Better after a frost, or in a pie.

name: Hazelnuts
desc: Cobnuts from the hedge. The squirrels had first dibs and they want you to know it.

name: Elderflower
desc: Creamy flat-topped blossom that smells like summer and, slightly, of cat.

name: Wild Garlic
desc: Ramsons from a shady bank. You can smell the wood from three fields away.

name: Field Mushrooms
desc: Pink-gilled and popped up overnight after the rain. Only the ones you're sure of.

name: Seaweed
desc: Dulse and bladderwrack off the tideline. Salty, slippery and full of goodness, allegedly.

name: Heather Honey
desc: Dark, thick and tasting of the moor. The bees were busy; you were just lucky.

name: Nettles
desc: Young tops, picked with your sleeve over your hand. Mostly.

name: Slate Chips
desc: A thin grey flake from the tips. Rings like a bell when you tap it.

name: Peat
desc: A dark brick of old bog. Burns slow and smells like a Highland fireside.

name: Sheep Wool
desc: Snagged on a fence wire and free to a good home. Greasy, warm and a bit sheepy.

name: Hawthorn Berries
desc: Red haws from the May tree. Bread and cheese, the old folk called the leaves.

name: Rowan Berries
desc: Bright red berries from the mountain ash. Nothing bad crosses a rowan, so they say.

name: Sea Glass
desc: Frosted green glass, tumbled smooth by the sea. A rare find. Hold it up to the light.

name: Ammonite
desc: A curled stone shell, older than the hills it came out of. A rare find.

name: Truffle
desc: A knobbly black lump that smells extraordinary. Pigs would fight you for it. A rare find.

name: Honeycomb
desc: A wild bees' comb, dripping gold. You left them plenty. A rare find.
